content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm unable to connect online with my [product_name] [article_no]. I'm attempting to use [product_name] [product_name] [version_no] and an Ethernet cable, but I don't know the IP address of my device. Is it possible to connect like this or do I need a specific [product_name] cable? The MAC address appears to be E0-DC-A0-53-02-BD. Trying with MAC and a desired IP hasn't worked. Attached picture shows an error about different subnets, but both IPs (192.168.0.15 for my PC and 192.168.0.203 for [product_name]) should be in the same subnet. Any advice?
When connecting, click on the blue double arrow. If you get an error, close the window and make a screenshot. Using the double arrow, the software scans for available [product_name] devices.
Clicking the double arrow doesn't do anything. No error shows up and no devices appear in the list.
The list stays empty.
Maybe the problem is in the hardware type selection. Picture attached. What hardware type should be selected for the [article_no]?

Your device [article_no] is a [product_name] without display; for hardware selection, pick [product_name] [version_no]. [company_name] updated order numbers with the latest [product_name], causing confusion for users.
Should I enter the MAC address to search for the device? Which format is correct: 1) E0-DC-A0-53-02-BD, 2) E0:DC:A0:53:02:BD, or 3) E0DCA05302BD?

You can't search by MAC address, only by IP. You mentioned your device's IP is 192.168.0.203. On delivery, it should be 192.168.0.3. How did you change the IP without connecting if your device doesn't have a display?
I saw somewhere that the IP might be 192.168.0.203.
Why haven't you answered this question?
I wasn't able to change the IP address. I also tried connecting using 192.168.0.203.
As mentioned before, by default the IP is 192.168.0.3 with subnet mask 255.255.255.0. Unless you've changed it, this should be the setting.
Open Windows command prompt. Type in ipconfig /all and press enter. Take a screenshot of the result and upload it to the forum.
For my PC, the IP is 192.168.0.15, subnet mask 255.255.255.0, and default gateway is blank. I'm still unable to connect. Screenshot attached.

An IP scanner can help find your device if you're having trouble. I often use one (see link). Picture of scanner result attached. Networks can be tricky if settings aren't correct. Make sure IP address, subnet mask are right, and avoid duplicate IPs.
Here's the ipconfig /all screenshot.
Are you connecting the PC directly to [product_name], or going through a router? If directly, have you tried using a different Ethernet cable?
I'm connecting directly from my PC to [product_name] using regular Ethernet cables, not crossover cables; I've tried two different ones.
Is it possible that a firewall is blocking ports? Have you tried disabling the firewall?
Can you try to ping [product_name]? For example: ping 192.168.0.3
The firewall is ON, and I don't have permission to turn it off. I'll ask the administrator tomorrow. Attached is a picture showing PING.
Are you on a company network? The firewall may be blocking access. As shown in your screenshot, [product_name] can't be reached by ping, meaning something is blocking the traffic.
Thanks, yes, I'm on a company network. I'll try disabling the firewall with help from IT tomorrow. For now, I just need a beer.
Have a beer for me too!
I've attached a section from the manual for the current [product_name] [version_no] about network security and the ports it uses.
Thanks for sharing the manual, [user_name]. It'll help when dealing with the IT department.

Hi, I wasn't able to turn off the firewall yet. I tried connecting the same PC to a [product_name] [version_no] [article_no] instead, and it worked! Is it possible for the firewall to block communication with [product_name] but not with [product_name] [version_no]?
I doubt it. If I were you, I’d open a support request.

I linked an IP scanner earlier; did you try scanning the whole 192.168.0.x range? It's possible your [product_name]'s IP conflicts with another device. Use the scanner or ping suspected addresses, but disconnect [product_name] from the network first. If nothing responds, those addresses are free.
Hi [user_name], I tried your IP scanner. No results. Only my PC and [product_name] are connected—no other network devices.

What do you mean by 'no results'? Was only the PC found? You can also scan areas beyond 192.168.0.x, though it may take longer depending on settings. I haven't had such issues with my [product_name] controllers. Can you try a different PC or laptop?
Did you follow my advice to start a support request?
Only the PC was found. I scanned 192.168.0.1 to .254 and 192.168.1.1 to .254, with two computers, but only my PC was detected.
Not yet. I'm attempting support now.
I've sent a support request.
I've sent a support request.

I think the problem is likely on the PC side, not with [product_name]. Support won't help much without full info about your PC hardware, software, and configuration. You need a systematic approach to troubleshoot—there are online resources and tools for each step. Alternatively, provide detailed steps so others might assist.
PROBLEM SOLVED! The correct IP was 192.168.2.1, though I don’t know how. After scanning different IP ranges, I found it. Thanks everyone!
That means your [product_name] was not in its default state, since someone must have changed the IP address.
I bought it new in the original packaging, but at this point, it's not important.
Systematic troubleshooting usually helps, though not always. Don't forget to check current settings, and good luck with your project!
Maybe [company_name] pre-set a different IP address for new devices. I also had a [product_name] [version_no], and its default IP was 192.168.0.3.

Even with an IP of 192.168.2.1, [product_name] [product_name] should have detected [product_name] by scanning with the double arrow. I have 192.168.178.27 on my PC, reset [product_name] to factory settings (IP 192.168.0.3), and [product_name] found it right away. Your issue is unusual.

The original [product_name] had IP 192.168.0.1, and later versions changed to 192.168.0.3. I haven't seen other defaults on new units. Maybe the initial [product_name] program was set to 192.168.2.1 and overwritten during transfer. Sometimes users overlook confirmation dialogs.
Regardless, [product_name] software should have found the device when scanning. Who knows what really caused it.

Even with the device at 192.168.2.1 and my PC at 192.168.2.15, the blue double arrow couldn’t find [product_name]. Setting device to 192.168.0.3 and PC to 192.168.0.15 also didn’t work—the list remained empty. But I was able to download the program. Now, I need to connect [product_name] to an HMI panel [article_no] (4 inch). I may need help again soon!

Did you see my last screenshot? I tested with IP 192.168.2.1 and [product_name] software detected the device by scanning with the blue double arrows, no problem. I transferred a program successfully; the PC created a temporary subnet. I can make a screen video if you want.
Screen video attached.
I've tried all these steps over the past several days. In my setup, the blue double arrow never works. Maybe there are still firewall issues. Wishing you a great weekend!
Same to you. Take care.

Sometimes you need to re-enter the PC’s static IP address. I've fixed communication issues by doing this. You can also check the IP of devices with a display model—it’s very helpful to have a display.
I've had antivirus software block communication with TCP-Modbus RTU servers as well. Once antivirus was disabled, connection worked fine.

analysis.insight_summary: Users experience confusion and difficulties connecting a new [product_name] without display over Ethernet, mainly because of uncertain default network settings like IP address and hardware type. Misunderstandings happen due to unclear product numbering, lack of easy network parameter discovery or reset, and ambiguous error messages in the software. These connection issues leave users unsure about necessary accessories and next troubleshooting steps.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a straightforward method to discover and connect to a new [product_name] via Ethernet, without specialized network knowledge, cables, or manual setup. They also want accurate hardware selection guidance and clear instructions for establishing the first connection.
